statement: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. Proves that for every real shift γ and finite-valued $`\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)`$, divergence of $`\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q`$ implies $`\|qx-\gamma\|\lt \psi(q)`$ for infinitely many q, for almost every x. Here ϕ is Euler's totient and the norm is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators are unrestricted; no monotonicity or Diophantine condition on γ is needed.
